# NBA Terminal ESPN session extension

This first-party extension reuses ESPN login in **the Firefox or Chromium profile already signed in**, after your explicit permission. It reads only SWID and espn_s2, sends them via an isolated content script's same-origin request to your paired local NBA Terminal app, and validates league access. No passwords, verification codes, cookie copying, remote cookie service, roster writes, or page-message credential channel. Sign in and complete MFA/CAPTCHA directly at ESPN.

## One-time installation and pairing

1. Start NBA Terminal on loopback. Download **firefox.zip** or **chromium.zip** from `/api/fantasy/espn/bridge/setup/` on that app origin. From a source checkout the same artifacts are in `nba_terminal/browser_extension/dist/`. Rebuild with `uv run python nba_terminal/browser_extension/build.py`.
2. **Firefox 128+:** open `about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox`, choose **Load Temporary Add-on**, select `firefox.zip` (or extract and choose manifest.json). This is an unsigned development install and Firefox removes it at browser restart. Reload it after restart. A permanent regular Firefox install requires Mozilla signing; no package is signed and no browser security preference is bypassed. Use the profile/container where ESPN is already signed in. Pin the extension button if helpful.
3. **Chromium 120+:** extract `chromium.zip` into a retained folder, open `chrome://extensions`, enable visible **Developer mode**, choose **Load unpacked**, select that folder. No web-store install or silent provider trust change occurs.
4. Reload the NBA Terminal tab after installation so its isolated content script is active. In NBA Terminal's ESPN setup enter league ID, ending season year (2026–27 means 2027), optional owned team, and explicitly start browser pairing. Then with **that local app tab active**, click this extension's toolbar button. Read the consent, click **Allow ESPN session for this local app**, and approve the browser's ESPN cookie/host permission dialog. Consent binds to the exact localhost origin (scheme, hostname, port), this browser profile and cookie store/container.
5. Existing ESPN login is checked immediately, including a login in another ESPN tab in this profile/store. If missing, use **Sign in directly at ESPN** in the popup; finish verification there. Leave an NBA Terminal tab open. Cookie changes trigger rechecks; a one-minute fallback poll handles missed events. ESPN league reads happen only on changed cookies, missing app session or hourly renewal, with five-minute error backoff. The app UI polls its authenticated status; extension page events are advisory only.
6. Select your owned team in NBA Terminal if not selected. Team selection is retained by the backend across cookie refreshes. No team guess is made when selection is ambiguous.

The normal supported extension origins are localhost and 127.0.0.1 over HTTP/HTTPS; use one consistently. The default normal cookie store is supported in Chromium; Firefox containers are matched to the local tab's store and the login tab opens in the same container. Separate profiles/incognito stores are intentionally not silently searched. ESPN cookies must be available to `https://www.espn.com/`; unusual partitioned/path-scoped deployments may require manual fallback.

## Disconnect, account changes and storage

NBA Terminal **Disconnect/Cancel/Forget** invalidates the bridge binding, outstanding refresh and current app session; no reconnect until you pair again. The extension popup **Forget this local app and disconnect** deletes consent for that origin and asks its active local tab to disconnect. If that request fails, use Disconnect in the app when available. For every local origin you used, disconnect separately; browser permission removal/uninstallation removes future cookie access but cannot erase an already delivered backend session while no app tab is open. Disconnect before uninstalling. Signing out at ESPN while an app tab remains open revokes the app session on the cookie change/poll.

An ESPN account change stops automatic renewal and invalidates the local session. Explicitly Disconnect, pair again, and re-enable the extension for the new intended account; it never silently adopts another account. Missing/expired/rejected cookies are reported without fake authentication success. Manual cookie entry remains available.

ESPN cookies are held only by the browser's existing cookie store and transient extension/content-script/backend memory. They are never written to extension storage, page DOM, localStorage, logs, URLs or clipboard. Extension `storage.local` stores only consent metadata: local origin, random non-secret consent generation, cookie-store ID and SHA-256 account identifier (not a bearer credential). This metadata is readable by this installed extension/profile and is cleared with Forget; the account hash is privacy-sensitive metadata, not encrypted OS storage. Backend random HttpOnly SameSite=Strict pairing/session capabilities are scoped to `/api/fantasy/espn`; pairing is valid up to 30 days in a single process, with no credentials on disk. Backend restart needs fresh pairing; Firefox temporary install needs reload after browser restart. Eight-hour app sessions are renewed hourly while active; no fixed ESPN session lifetime is promised.

## Validation and restrictions

Automated tests mock browser APIs and ESPN responses; they exercise real bridge routes and session ownership/CSRF/replay/revocation logic. They do **not** establish live private ESPN compatibility. No consenting real-account test has been performed. In this implementation environment an isolated Firefox WebDriver smoke attempt exited before session creation and web-ext lint exited 138 without validation output; automated package/schema checks passed but are not a real-browser validation. Browser install/permission prompts remain real user steps. ESPN may change cookie/API behavior; use manual fallback if refused. No challenge bypass or password capture is implemented.

Browser API references: [Mozilla cookies](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/cookies), [user-gesture permission requests](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/API/permissions/request), [Chrome isolated content scripts](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/develop/concepts/content-scripts), [Firefox temporary loading](https://extensionworkshop.com/documentation/develop/temporary-installation-in-firefox/). Verified during implementation 2026-10-31.

Run `bun test nba_terminal/browser_extension/tests` for extension mocks, `uv run pytest tests/test_espn_bridge.py` for bounded backend tests. The package includes both unsigned ZIP artifacts and these installation instructions; the API serves only the three fixed allowlisted setup filenames.
